newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani rupee ends lower in kerb, seen stable.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani rupee ends lower in kerb, seen stable.

text.p: The Pakistani rupee ended 0.02 lower at 41.22 to the dollar in the kerb market on Wednesday amid balanced demand and supply of the U.S. currency, dealers said.
The rupee is likely to open stable on Friday after May Day holiday on Thursday, one dealer said.
The State (central) Bank of Pakistan rate, last changed on April 23, was 40.2400/40.4412 to the dollar.
The premium on foreign exchange bearer certificates closed at 2.60 percent compared to the opening at 2.50 percent.
